library_preparation_preflight.summary: JavaCPP presets split native binaries into a sibling '-platform' artifact (repo convention for all org.bytedeco libs); also, librealsense v1 is a physical USB RealSense camera driver with no documented software-only/mock-device mode, so CI coverage is inherently capped to no-device/error paths.

deterministic_setup.reason: Base artifact contains only JNI glue, no native binaries; every bytedeco preset (see openblas, tesseract in this repo) needs the matching '-platform' artifact at test runtime or native-image run fails with UnsatisfiedLinkError.

library_preparation_preflight.agent_guidance: This library wraps the legacy librealsense (v1) SDK for Intel RealSense depth cameras; context.get_device_count() will return 0 and context.get_device(n) is unusable in CI since no physical USB camera is attached. Write tests around context construction, device-count/no-device-found paths, and any pure API surface (error codes, enum/constant access) that doesn't require an actual connected device. Do not write tests that assume a device is present — they will fail deterministically in this environment, not flakily.
risks: Coverage ceiling is low and setup cannot raise it: no Docker image or env var can simulate a physical USB RealSense camera, so real frame-capture/streaming code paths are permanently unreachable here.

librealsense v1 is superseded upstream by librealsense2, which does support recording/playback pseudo-devices; this older API lacks that option, so there's no in-library fallback for hardware-free testing.
